title.en: Homes and Cars: Technologies, Citizens and the Energy Transition (100)

fullTitle.en: Homes and Cars: Technologies, Citizens and the Energy Transition (100)

goals.en:
Upon the successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
- Understand practices of mobility, consumption and home-making in relation to energy and sustainability
- Understand the interactions between different infrastructural systems of energy generation, transmission, and storage, mobility and transportation and housing
- Analyze the potential of citizen participation in energy transition on basis of different models.
- Assess the place and scale of the personal sphere in relation to energy transition
- Evaluate the appropriateness of approaches to energy transition (modelling, practice-based, action research and multi-level perspective) for reaching different goals

description.en:
The course aims to discuss recent developments and innovations in the area of energy (such as new forms of heating, storage, electric vehicles and car-sharing), in relation to basic energy needs in housing and transportation. The course addresses challenges in integrating practice-based research on energy and new approaches to energy use at the level of socio-technical systems. The course will also be part of the week of the region. 

In particular, the course will address the Sustainable Development Goals 7 Affordable and Clean Energy, Goal 11 Sustainable Cities and Communities, Goal 12 Responsible Consumption and production, and to some extent Goal 13 Climate Action.

This 100-level course will further enrich the theoretical baggage with a third approach to energy research (practice theory and action research). The course builds on major themes in other courses of the program including:
- interaction between economic, behavioural and technological factors
- use of futuring, scenarios and foresight approaches for mobilizing change
- understanding of systems, their features and interactions
- understanding of different approaches to sustainability
